plan.disposition: Mini-Plan reviewed inside the iterate spec by spec-reviewer across three Stage-1 rounds (it is a spec section, not a separate artifact). No separate --mode plan run: the external-review budget went to --mode code, which is the stronger check for a BUG-path change whose plan is seven mechanical steps and whose entire risk is in the code. Skill rule: external LLM review at medium+ — satisfied in code mode, recorded under external_code.

findings.finding: has_header still did a strict read_text one call BEFORE the write that was fixed, so ensure_header still raised UnicodeDecodeError - and the diff's own comment claimed the class had been removed from that module. Made MORE reachable by the (then) lenient writer, which could persist a byte the strict reader refuses.

Flipping durable_read_text's DEFAULT to surrogateescape was a fail-open regression with NO beneficiary: no triage-store reader goes through it, while all four real callers json.loads a run-config file where config_io maps JSONDecodeError to {} - read by its caller as 'first run, no config yet'.
Six bare run_git calls remained on the 15s default, two of them INSIDE the canonical lock in the operator's MAIN tree, where a killed process strands .git/index.lock.
A module-level 'from lib.git_base import run_git' in a shared/scripts top-level module is the ADR-045 anti-pattern, and the justifying comment inverted the lazy mitigation it claimed to mirror.
test_git_diff_is_bounded_and_utf8 asserted NEITHER property in its name - it stubbed run_git, which is where both live, and captured a timeout value it never asserted.
The header EOL was decoupled from the appender's on Windows, and has_header read the WHOLE append-only log to inspect line 1 on every tracked append.

Claim under doubt: AC-6: _op_in_progress answers yes when it cannot tell — The rebase-merge / rebase-apply / BISECT_LOG loop treated TIMEOUT_RETURNCODE as 'continue', so a timeout returned False and the sweep would commit into an in-progress rebase - where the old bare run_git crashed loudly. A rebase sets NONE of the pseudo-refs the first loop checks, so the second loop is the only detector. The existing test patched every call to 124, so the first loop short-circuited and the second never executed.

Claim under doubt: the surrogateescape ENCODE only affects input that would otherwise have raised — durable_atomic_write has ~35 callers writing git-tracked JSON that is read back strictly, none with a repair pass. A lone surrogate would silently persist invalid UTF-8 and relocate the crash to every future reader. The beneficiary analysis applied to the read side was never applied to the write side.

Claim under doubt: AC-7 is additive for F1 — HEAD~1..HEAD on a one-commit or shallow repo exits 128 -> error -> F1 failed -> the whole finalization bundle aborts, for a repo whose only sin is being new.

Claim under doubt: the deferred _append_line change is out of scope for AC-2 — _append_line wrote os.linesep, so on Windows the AC-2 benefit lasted exactly one append before reconcile rewrote the whole log. Row 48's test asserted os.linesep on both sides - a tautology that would have gone RED once the code became correct.
Claim under doubt: ledger rows 44 and 49 are tested — No test drove _has_drift or _head_line_set to None, and none raised ImportError from the lazy seam; the cited tests hit neighbouring branches.

Claim under doubt: detect_drift always returns a structured result — _nothing_to_compare_against made three run_git calls OUTSIDE the try/except - reintroducing the very hole the ImportError widening had just closed, one statement later.

Claim under doubt: the _append_line EOL change is covered — Measured: this repo's tracked store is 1145/1145 CRLF, and only a FRESH store was tested. Every reader was traced and could not be broken - a coverage gap on the most load-bearing write, not a defect.

external_code.raw_excerpt:
External code review — openrouter (gpt-5.6-terra + gemini-3.1-pro-preview), 4 rounds.

GPT (success in 3 of 4 rounds) raised 6 actionable findings, ALL addressed:
R1: (a) `_nothing_to_compare_against` downgraded a typo'd ref to a no-op, reintroducing
    the false-clean AC-7 closes. (b) the AC-9 CI-routing tests ran on a plain tmp_path
    where should_route_to_outbox already returns False via the no-origin path, so they
    passed with OR without the guard — measured and confirmed vacuous.
R2: (c) `HEAD~bogus` — a MALFORMED suffix on a resolvable base still slipped through
    the base-resolution check.
R3: (d) detect_drift caught FileNotFoundError but not other OSError (a non-runnable
    git raises PermissionError). (e) `_has_drift` special-cased only TIMEOUT_RETURNCODE,
    so any other non-zero `git status` left stdout empty and reported a confident
    "no drift" from an unanswered probe.

DISCARDED as subset artifacts, not acted on: R3 also claimed "the diff adds only
_f1_record tests" and R4 returned only "AC-N is not implemented (no change in diff)"
findings. Both are true of the SLICE and false of the change — the documented
narrowed-diff failure mode. Labelled rather than actioned.

Gemini: DEGRADED in all 4 rounds (finish_reason=length — reply-side truncation, not
input size; narrowing the diff did not help). Not counted as a pass. Its two quoted
blocks were hand-inspected instead: (1) the GC survivor rewrite's handling of a
concurrently appended line — it is not in `quarantined_text`, so it survives, which is
AC-3 and is pinned by test_append_during_commit_window_is_not_deleted_by_the_gc
(verified RED first); (2) blank lines surviving when nothing else changed — true,
harmless (every reader skips blank lines), and unchanged from the pre-diff gate.
